newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-FORMER CHAMPIONS STRUGGLE TO AVOID FRENCH FATE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-FORMER CHAMPIONS STRUGGLE TO AVOID FRENCH FATE.

text.p: The United States, Germany and Sweden, all Davis Cup winners in the last four years, face a final day test of nerve to avoid joining holders France as first round casualties.

French celebrations in Malmo nine weeks ago seemed a distant memory in Sydney as Australian pair Mark Woodforde and Todd Woodbridge completed a straight sets win over Guy Forget and Guillaume Raoux in Saturday's doubles to send the defending champions crashing out.

Germany, winners in 1993, will follow them unless they can win both reverse singles against Spain on clay in Mallorca, and neither the U.S. nor Sweden are home and dry despite 2-1 leads over less-fancied opposition.
American hopes of wrapping up their awkward tie in Brazil were dashed when Jaime Oncins and Gustavo Kuerten outplayed Alex O'Brien and Richey Reneberg in the doubles to win 6-2 6-4 7-5.

The Americans admitted they failed to perform to their normal standards in front of a 5,000-strong crowd in Ribeirao Preto who greeted the U.S. pair with a chorus of whistling, and blew horns and pounded samba drums between points.
"My brain was on that drum up in the stands, my forehand was in the field outside the court, my serve was back in Texas and my backhand was in Sao Paulo," said a disappointed O'Brien afterwards.

Swedish pair Nicklas Kulti and Mikael Tillstrom also experienced their fair share of pressure against Switzerland, finally subduing Marc Rosset and Lorenzo Manta in five sets to take a slender advantage into Sunday's singles.

Apart from Australia, relishing their return to World Group tennis after a gap of two years, the only other definite winners on Saturday were Italy who took an unbeatable 3-0 lead over Mexico in Rome.

South Africa are well placed to join them in the second round after Wayne Ferreira edged out Russia's Andrei Cherkasov in a delayed singles rubber which developed into another five-set marathon in fierce heat and humidity in Durban.

Marcos Ondruska had showed his compatriot the way the previous day with a dramatic victory over Andrei Chesnokov, and Ferreira duly triumphed 7-5 6-3 3-6 4-6 8-6 in an encounter lasting four hours and 20 minutes.

Saturday's scheduled doubles match between South Africa's Ellis Ferreira and Grant Stafford and Cherkasov and Andrei Olhovsky was postponed until Sunday morning to allow the 26-year-old Russian time to recover
Elsewhere, the late inclusion of Petr Korda in the Czech Republic's doubles team failed to prevent Leander Paes and Mahesh Bhupathi giving India a surprise 2-1 lead in their tie in Pribram.
The Indian pair won 7-6 6-3 6-4 as Czech captain Vladislav Savrda's last minute switch failed to pay dividends for last year's semifinalists.

The Netherlands also gave themselves a possible escape route in Bucharest where Paul Haarhuis and Jacco Eltingh beat Romanian second-string Ion Moldovan and Razvan Sabau to reduce their team's deficit to 2-1.
No-one was more philosophical, though, than French captain Yannick Noah, having seen Australia's famous 'Woodies' expertly dismantle French expectations on grass in high temperatures at White City.
"Last year we won after a wonderful ride and a beautiful mystery," said Noah. "Now this is reality."
